Can you elaborate on what you mean by "blocks the current thread"?  This might be a misunderstanding.

If you're using the async sdbusplus bindings, you can `co_await libspdm_stuff(...)` and the _thread_ isn't blocked, but the request is not answered until the full co-routine completes.  This allows the daemon to service other dbus requests in the meantime.

I have no idea what you mean by "Change D-Bus API to return task".  You can't change the YAML to return a task.  A task is a co-routine.  You can't send a co-routine across processes.

```
Option 1: Change D-Bus API to Return sdbusplus::async::task<>
Co_await on the function which does the libspdm_stuff

eg:
auto spdmGetSignedMeasurements(
std::vector<size_t> measurementIndices,
std::string nonce,
size_t slotId) -> sdbusplus::async::task<std::tuple<sdbusplus::message::object_path, std::string, std::string, std::string, std::string, std::string>>
```

This is code from the generated bindings in `xyz/openbmc_project/Attestation/MeasurementSet/aserver.hpp`: https://gist.github.com/williamspatrick/4dc6bed5e6370b806b27a9bc00ccdd9c

You need to implement a method call `auto method_call(spdm_get_signed_measurements_t, ...)` that either returns the `tuple` (sync, blocking) or the `task<tuple>` (async, nonblocking) and the bindings automatically do the right thing.  If that method_call returns a task, the message handling for the method call becomes async.

The sdbusplus examples have this exact scenario: https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/master/example/calculator-aserver.cpp#L14 .  `multiple` is implemented as a synchronous method, `divide` is implemented as an asynchronous method.

Is spawning a thread to make libspdm asynchronous a good idea? This approach introduces concerns about synchronized access to globals like `ctx`, which can make the code slower and harder to debug. Are you using threads due to limitations in the libspdm API? Does libspdm support non-blocking socket mode? If so, you could leverage that feature to avoid spawning threads.

>Is spawning a thread to make libspdm asynchronous a good idea?
Can you propose some other solution, considering the libspdm API is synchronus?

After reviewing the libspdm code, it appears that it is not currently designed for asynchronous programming. If MCTP and DOE sockets support non-blocking modes, we could potentially leverage this to create an asynchronous SPDM library. Since the workload is mostly I/O bound, a single-threaded (main thread) approach could be used to implement concurrent measurement processes. However, the existing SPDM APIs do not seem to support this model. Specifically, `spdm_device_send_message` would need to be converted into a coroutine function, which would require rewriting it in C++ using either `sdbusplus::context` or `asio::context`.

I'm also uncertain whether using threads, as you have suggested, would result in a cleaner solution. Is `spdm_context` designed to be thread-safe? Can we perform parallel measurement retrievals using a single `spdm_context` instance? Personally, I would prefer the asynchronous approach over a threading-based solution.
